newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada says no new aluminum MOU in the works.
newsitem.headline: Canada says no new aluminum MOU in the works.

text.p: A Canadian government spokesman on Friday said there were no plans to renew a two-year global deal on cutting aluminum output that expired earlier this year.

"The MOU (memorandum of understanding) was done for specific purpose at the time, for two years and they (the countries) feel that it accomplished its goals. There will not be another MOU, simply a working group," International Trade Department spokesman Sanjeev Chowdhury told Reuters.

Chowdhury said representatives of Industry Canada will be travelling to Russia the week of October 21 for a working group meeting to discuss the resumption of the publication of regular aluminum production statistics which had ceased after the original MOU expired.

"All the other countries have agreed to participate in this working group. Russia is indicating that it is simply a formality and Canadian representatives are going to meet with them during the week of October 21," he said.
"Provided everything goes as planned, we should begin publishing statistics again in November or December," Chowdhury added.
The first global agreement was signed in March 1994 by major producers Russia, Australia, Canada, the European Union, Norway and the United States.
Earlier on Friday, a Russian aluminum executive said Russia's top aluminum producers may agree to curb production.
-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
